note: Which sentences of the reference note support each target. Sentences are identified by a phrase they contain, so the file survives the note being re-prepared. 'gold' is the main source in the acute primary angle closure section; 'alsoSupports' is other text that backs the point; 'distractor' mentions the same words about something else.

gold: a sudden symptomatic rise in IOP caused by angle closure
A narrow angle in the other eye, which is an important diagnostic clue
Shallow chamber, fixed mid-dilated pupil, narrow angle in the other eye
alsoSupports: Dim light, such as a cinema or a dark room
Drugs with anticholinergic effects, including some antihistamines
A fixed, mid-dilated, often vertically oval pupil
Very high IOP, usually 50 to 80 mmHg

gold: so pilocarpine works better once the pressure has started to fall
alsoSupports: The aims are to lower the IOP quickly
Hyperosmotic agents if the pressure stays high

gold: Check for sulfonamide allergy, kidney disease, low potassium and sickle cell disease before giving it
distractor: Avoid acetazolamide, which is itself a sulfonamide
Stevens–Johnson syndrome; sulfonamide allergy, kidney disease, sickle cell disease

gold: Any trigger drug should be stopped and the patient warned about others
Drugs with anticholinergic effects, including some antihistamines
distractor: Stop the drug (with the prescriber) and use cycloplegics

gold: Laser peripheral iridotomy (LPI) in the affected eye once the cornea has cleared
Prophylactic LPI in the fellow eye, because without treatment
alsoSupports: the priority is prompt iridotomy in both eyes
After acute primary angle closure, in both eyes

gold: Once the eye has settled, repeat gonioscopy
Prophylactic LPI in the fellow eye, because without treatment
alsoSupports: the priority is prompt iridotomy in both eyes
A narrow angle in the other eye, which is an important diagnostic clue

gold: The iris sphincter is often ischaemic and does not respond while the IOP is very high
Early laser iridotomy, after clearing the cornea with topical glycerol
Laser peripheral iridoplasty to pull the peripheral iris away from the angle
Hyperosmotic agents if the pressure stays high
Review the diagnosis, for example aqueous misdirection
alsoSupports: Anterior chamber paracentesis as a temporary measure
Surgical peripheral iridectomy, early lens extraction

unsupported: Arrange an urgent MRI of the brain and orbits
Start high-dose oral prednisolone for giant cell arteritis
Check the HbA1c and start metformin
